newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban tells Iran not to fuel conflict.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban tells Iran not to fuel conflict.

text.p: The Taleban Islamic movement, told Iran on Monday that helping its rivals would only "pour petrol on the flames" of the Afghan conflict.
A statement from Taleban, which rules most of Afghanistan, also accused Iran of blocking Afghan merchandise at Islam Qala border post and called for the release of the detained consignments.

A Taleban supreme council chaired by the movement's chief, Mullah Mohammad Omar, in the southern town of Kandahar considered "Iranian interference" in Afghanistan's internal affairs, a Taleban spokesman told the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press.
"The council asked Iran not to sprinkle petrol on the flames in Afghanistan and desist from helping anti-government forces," spokesman Mullah Said Mohammad Haqqani said.
The Taleban, which captured the capital Kabul in late September, accuses Iran of supporting the ousted government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani. Tehran still recognises him but denies the charge.
